facts.text: Placards assert rights: 'Education is our right', the assurance of a minimum wage, and a right over forests and their resources.
facts.quote: Education is our right. ... We must get the assurance of a minimum wage. It is our right! ... We have a right over our forests and its resources!

facts.text: We get rights at birth; every newborn baby has a right to live.
facts.quote: We get rights at birth. Every newborn baby has a right to live.

facts.text: Only with protection from injustice, exploitation, discrimination and deprivation can individuals develop their skills and qualities.
facts.quote: Only when all individuals get protection from injustice, exploitation, discrimination and deprivation, will they be able to develop their skills and qualities.

facts.text: The Constitution guaranteed equal rights to all citizens to create a conducive atmosphere; these are fundamental rights.
facts.quote: The Indian Constitution has guaranteed equal rights to all citizens in order to create this conducive atmosphere. These rights are fundamental rights.

facts.text: Being included in the Constitution, fundamental rights have the status of law and everybody must abide by them.
facts.quote: As they are included in the Constitution, they have the status of law. It is imperative for everybody to abide by these rights.

facts.text: Right to Equality: the State cannot discriminate as superior-inferior or men-women; the same law applies equally to all.
facts.quote: According to the right to equality, the State cannot discriminate among citizens as superior-inferior or as men-women and cannot give different treatment or privileges to anybody. The same law applies equally to all.

facts.text: We have protection from arrest without warrant, and the State cannot discriminate while extending such protection.
facts.quote: For example, we have protection from arrest without warrant. Also the State cannot discriminate while extending such protection.

facts.text: For government employment the State cannot discriminate on grounds of religion, caste, race, sex, descent, place of birth or residence.
facts.quote: The State cannot discriminate against any citizen on grounds of religion, caste, race, sex, descent or place of birth or residence for government employment.

facts.text: Untouchability has been abolished by law; practising it in any form is a cognizable offence; it was abolished to establish equality.
facts.quote: The inhuman practice of untouchability that was prevalent in our country has been abolished by law. The practice of untouchability in any form is a cognizable offence. This practice has been abolished in order to establish equality in Indian society.

facts.text: Titles that create an artificial hierarchy, like Raja, Maharaja and Raobahadur, have been abolished.
facts.quote: The Constitution has also abolished titles that create an artificial hierarchy among people. For example, titles like Raja, Maharaja, Raobahadur, etc. have been abolished.

facts.text: The State confers awards like Padmashree, Padmabhushan and Padmavibhushan for distinguished contribution in different fields.
facts.quote: But the State does confer awards like Padmashree, Padmabhushan, Padmavibhushan, etc. for distinguished contribution in different fields.

facts.text: Bharat Ratna is the greatest civilian honour or award of our country.
facts.quote: Bharat Ratna is the greatest civilian honour or award of our country.

facts.text: Paramveer Chakra, Ashok Chakra and Shaurya Chakra are awarded for remarkable service in the armed forces.
facts.quote: Medals of honour like Paramveer Chakra, Ashok Chakra, Shaurya Chakra are awarded for remarkable service in the armed forces.

facts.text: Such awards don't bestow any special rights or privileges; they are only a recognition of contribution.
facts.quote: Such awards don't bestow any special rights or privileges upon those who receive them. It is only a recognition of their contribution.

facts.text: The Right to Liberty guarantees all the freedoms necessary from the point of view of the individual.
facts.quote: Right to Liberty : This is a very important right given by the Constitution. It gives a guarantee of all the freedoms necessary from the point of view of the individual.

facts.text: Freedoms: speech and expression; to assemble peaceably; to form associations or unions; to move freely throughout India.
facts.quote: freedom of speech and expression - freedom to assemble peaceably - freedom to form associations or unions - freedom to move freely throughout the territory of India.

facts.text: Freedoms: to reside and settle in any part of India; to practise any lawful profession, occupation, trade or business.
facts.quote: freedom to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India. - freedom to practise any lawful profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade or business of one's choice.

facts.text: 'A' established the 'Adivasi Cooperation Forum'; 'B' moved his father's bakery production from Goa to Maharashtra; 'C' wrote an article on the new tax policy.
facts.quote: 'A' established 'Adivasi Cooperation Forum' to solve the problems of the tribal people. 'B' decided to move his father's bakery production from Goa to Maharashtra. 'C' found some lacunae in the new tax policy of the Government. He wrote an article

facts.text: Rights must be exercised responsibly; freedom of expression does not allow speaking or writing anything that might incite violence.
facts.quote: But we have to exercise these responsibly. ... We have the freedom of expression but we cannot speak or write anything that might incite anybody to violence.

facts.text: The right to life implies a guarantee to live and a conducive environment for living; nobody can take away another's life.
facts.quote: we all have a right to life. It appears to be simple, but it has a deep significance. It implies getting a guarantee to live; availability of a conducive environment for living. Nobody can take away another's life.

facts.text: No person can be arrested and detained without any reason.
facts.quote: No person can be arrested and detained without any reason.

facts.text: A right supplementary to the right to life: nobody can be punished twice for the same offence.
facts.quote: There are some rights supplementary to the right to life. For example, nobody can be punished twice for the same offence.

facts.text: Allegations must be proved by the courts; the police collect evidence; even a person who accepts a crime is not punished immediately.
facts.quote: Before being punished, the allegations against a person have to be proved. The courts have to perform this task. The police collect evidence against the accused and put up the case in the court. Even if a person accepts that he has committed a crime, he is not punished immediately.

facts.text: The right to liberty now includes the Right to Education: all children between 6 and 14 years are entitled to education as a Fundamental Right.
facts.quote: The right to liberty now also includes the Right to Education. All children between 6 and 14 years of age are entitled to get education as a Fundamental Right.

facts.text: Right against Exploitation: children under 14 cannot be employed in hazardous places, factories or mines.
facts.quote: it is prohibited to employ children under 14 years of age in hazardous places. Children cannot be employed or made to work in factories and mines.

facts.text: Exploitation includes bonded labour, forced work, treating somebody like a slave, denying legitimate compensation, excessive work, starving or ill-treating.
facts.quote: Exploitation includes bonded labour or forcing somebody to work against his/her wish, treating somebody like a slave, denying them legitimate compensation, making them do excessive or strenuous work, starving them or ill-treating them.

facts.text: Generally women, children, the weaker sections and powerless people are exploited; this right helps us stand up against exploitation.
facts.quote: Generally women, children, the weaker sections of society and powerless people are exploited. This right enables us to stand up against any kind of exploitation.

facts.text: Boards in shops and hotels read 'Children are not employed here' and 'Workers are paid daily here'.
facts.quote: Children are not employed here. Workers are paid daily here. You see such boards in shops and hotels.

facts.text: The Minimum Wages Act has provisions relating to working hours and rest hours in factories.
facts.quote: Minumum Wages Act - Provisions relating to working hours, rest hours, etc. in factories.

facts.text: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act is another law made to prevent exploitation.
facts.quote: The Government has made many laws in order to prevent exploitation ... The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act

facts.text: The Right against Exploitation has a special provision to prevent the exploitation of children.
facts.quote: While the Constitution has banned all types of oppression through the right against exploitation, it has made a special provision to prevent the exploitation of children.

facts.text: The legal protection of the right to liberty is given to everybody equally and not denied to anybody.
facts.quote: This legal protection has been given to everybody equally. It is not denied to anybody.
